svg.text: 4 × 6 cm perfboard (14 × 20 holes), top view, drawn to scale. The ESP32's USB-C end hangs off the SHORT edge that faces the case's back wall.
Row 1: display L + display C (7-pin each).
The ESP32's antenna end hovers over rows 3–5.
Inputs side: D34 light sensor, D32/D33/D25/D26
switches, D13 LED. R1, R2, and the 2-pin
LDR / LED plugs go in cols 1–2.
Display side: D23, D22, D21, D18, D5,
Most display wiring runs to rows 1–2 underneath.
Long leg (+) → 3V3 row 20, stripe (−) → GND row 19,
bridged over to the right header column
⑤ THIS EDGE → CASE BACK WALL
USB-C sticks out ~3 mm past the board edge.
Line it up with the case's USB-C cutout.
SIDE VIEW — how the overhang meets the case wall
case floor · M3 standoffs + heat-set inserts
push both female header strips onto the ESP32 first, set it on the board at columns 3 and 13, then solder. The spacing comes out exact.
your board's pin rows are 10 holes apart (1.0"), which is why it only leaves one side free on the breadboard. So use columns 3 and 13.
viewed from the top with USB-C toward you, VIN/GND/D13 are on the LEFT and 3V3/GND/D15 on the RIGHT, the same as the wiring diagram.
the female headers lift it ~8.5 mm, so low parts (resistors, jumper wires) can also go underneath.
